comparisons.title: ChatGPT vs Claude
comparisons.decisionQuestion: Which individual paid plan fits the work you repeat?
comparisons.summary: Both entry paid plans cost $20 on monthly billing. Choose after running the same real task in each; annual commitment is a separate decision.
comparisons.recommendationBasis: Editorial judgment from documented plan fit; no comparative hands-on quality test.

choose.when: Your recurring task works well in its available tools and the result survives a factual check.
choose.avoid: You need a team workspace or guaranteed fixed task volume from this individual plan.

choose.when: Your document or writing trial produces useful output with fewer corrections for your own workload.
choose.avoid: An annual discount is the only reason to commit before testing your task.

trialChecklist: Use the same non-sensitive brief, source files and output requirements in both tools.
Include one exception, one missing fact and one instruction to preserve exact numbers.
Record factual errors, edits required and time to an acceptable output. Repeat on three different tasks.
Record model, plan and date; do not treat one successful output as a reliability guarantee.

assumptions: Individual paid subscriptions only; one person per quoted plan.
A twelve-month projection is separate from an annual subscription offer.
caveats: Free plans, team plans, API usage, taxes and usage add-ons are outside these quotes.
No fixed message allowance or model-quality score is inferred.

comparisons.title: Zapier vs Make
comparisons.decisionQuestion: What does your workflow consume at the volume you expect?
comparisons.summary: Count billable actions and module executions separately. The same business outcome can use different numbers of tasks and credits.
comparisons.recommendationBasis: Editorial judgment from documented plan fit; no comparative hands-on quality test.

values.make: Credits used by modules; AI may consume more

values.zapier: 100 tasks; one action after a trigger
values.make: 1,000 credits; confirm scheduling and integration needs

choose.when: Its exact app actions cover the process and your measured task use fits the tier.
choose.avoid: You assume Free permits several action steps or premium apps.

choose.when: You can inspect and maintain a scenario and its measured module usage fits the credit allowance.
choose.avoid: You treat every completed workflow as one credit or ignore polling and fan-out.

trialChecklist: Build the same small sample using test records you control.
Run a normal record, a duplicate and a missing-field case; inspect the destination after each.
Read the actual usage logs and record tasks or credits separately.
Check retry behavior, duplicate prevention and what happens when the allowance is exhausted.

assumptions: Zapier estimate = runs × standard billable action steps.
Make estimate = runs × (standard action modules + trigger modules) + extra credits.
These are user-specified simple-run assumptions, not a platform equivalence benchmark.
caveats: Polling, bundles, loops, retries and AI can change consumption. Enter additional measured Make credits when known.
MCP, Lead Router, AI and extended code runtimes have different Zapier task rates.
Overages and larger plan tiers are not extrapolated; outside verified allowances, obtain a quote.

comparisons.decisionQuestion: Do you need a broadcast newsletter or an automated welcome series?
comparisons.summary: List size, total email sends and automation requirements decide whether a free plan fits. Count welcome emails as well as broadcasts.
comparisons.recommendationBasis: Editorial judgment from documented plan fit; no comparative hands-on quality test.

values.mailerlite: Up to 3 active automations, with 5 steps in each; sends share the monthly allowance.
values.kit: Paid plan required for sequences and visual automations

values.mailerlite: Comfort/Power quotes cover up to 500 subscribers
values.kit: Creator quote covers up to 1,000 subscribers

choose.when: A small list needs a controlled welcome series and its sends fit the allowance.
choose.avoid: You use a 500-subscriber quote to budget for a larger list.

choose.when: A broadcast-focused audience fits the Free scope, or Creator’s paid automation meets your requirements.
choose.avoid: You expect the 10,000-subscriber Free plan to run welcome sequences.

trialChecklist: Create a test subscriber and verify form consent and the confirmation behavior.
Send the intended sequence only to controlled test recipients.
Check tags, timing, unsubscribe behavior and whether a repeat signup restarts the workflow.
Calculate sends for broadcasts plus new subscribers entering the sequence; check actual billed subscriber count.
Count the largest automation including its delay and condition blocks; verify the plan cap independently of monthly sends.

assumptions: Estimated sends = active subscribers × full-list broadcasts + new sequence entrants × welcome emails.
Subscriber input is the expected peak active list including new subscribers; new entrants are a subset, not an extra charge added again.
All welcome emails are assumed sent within the same billing month.

The welcome sequence is modeled as one automation. Count all email, delay, condition and other action blocks in the largest automation, excluding the trigger. The default is 3 emails plus 2 delays = 5 steps.
caveats: Segmented sends, other sequences, tests and resends can change actual volume.
Above quoted subscriber tiers, no exact paid cost is produced.
Deliverability and business results were not benchmarked.

Step capacity is checked only when active automations are requested. The reviewed Kit sources do not establish a per-automation step cap; that capacity stays unverified rather than being treated as unlimited.

editorialStandards.title: Label the evidence actually collected
editorialStandards.rule: Separate official-documentation checks, worked examples and hands-on test records. Use a tested label only when the named task was performed and recorded.

editorialStandards.title: Publish the decision criteria
editorialStandards.rule: State the job, necessary features, exclusion criteria and price scope before recommending a plan. Recommendations remain editorial judgments.

editorialStandards.title: Do not manufacture scores
editorialStandards.rule: A rating needs defined inputs and a reproducible method. Vendor documentation alone does not produce a performance or customer-satisfaction score.

editorialStandards.title: Make prices comparable
editorialStandards.rule: Show billing unit, capacity, payment frequency, annual cash commitment, exclusions and checked date. Return unknown outside verified tiers.

editorialStandards.title: Give the reader a next step
editorialStandards.rule: Pair a shortlist with a realistic setup example and a small trial checklist that a reader can complete independently.

editorialStandards.title: Keep commercial status separate
editorialStandards.rule: An affiliate relationship does not establish suitability. Show limitations and do not let a commission substitute for evidence.
